definition_zh: 例如；比如；以……为例（引出一个实例来说明前文）
definition_en: used to introduce a single example that illustrates or supports what has just been said
core_image: 黑板上先写下一句通则，老师再用粉笔圈出一个具体例子
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一句通则，随后用粉笔圈出一个具体例子让学生看清。Helium and argon, for instance, hardly react with anything.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（引出一个实例来说明前面的总体陈述）；句意为氦与氩这类气体，例如它们，几乎不与任何物质发生反应。

pos.zh: 副词性短语：例如；比如；以……为例

collocations.phrase: for instance in the case of

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「在场、紧迫」的名词经法语进入英语，义为「实例；事例；情况」
由该名词加复数词尾构成，义为「多个实例」
由名词转作动词，义为「举……为例」（较正式）
由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「用实例表示；实例化」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词词尾构成，义为「实例化；例示」

senses.title: One illustrative example
senses.definition: to offer a single case that makes a general statement clear
senses.definitionCN: 提出一个具体事例，使前面的总体说法变得清楚
senses.example: Some metals resist sea air well; stainless steel, for instance, lasts for years on a pier.
senses.exampleCN: 有些金属很耐海风侵蚀，例如不锈钢，在码头上能用许多年。
senses.why: Instance names a single occurrence, and the phrase points at one such occurrence as proof of a wider claim.
senses.whyCN: 「实例」指单独发生的一件事，这个短语就指向其中一个实例，用来证明更宽泛的说法。

senses.title: Opening an illustrative passage
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to open a stretch of illustration after a general point
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，在提出总体观点之后开启一段例证
senses.example: For instance, a single cracked weld can close a whole pipeline.
senses.exampleCN: 例如，一道裂开的焊缝就能让整条管道停运。
senses.why: The phrase can stand first because the general point has already been placed in the sentence before.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语能站在句首，是因为总体观点已经由前一句立住了。

senses.title: Parenthetical single case
senses.definition: inserted between commas to name one case without interrupting the main clause
senses.definitionCN: 用逗号插入句中，点出一个例子而不打断主句
senses.example: The night staff, for instance the cleaners, were never told about the change.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班人员，例如清洁工，从未被告知这项变动。
senses.why: As a parenthesis the phrase adds a case without claiming to list every member.
senses.whyCN: 作为插入语，它只补上一个例子，并不声称已列尽所有成员。

senses.title: One case taken as representative
senses.definition: used after the verb take to single out one case as representative of a class
senses.definitionCN: 与表示「拿」的动词连用，从一类事物中单挑一个作为代表
senses.example: Take the oldest bridge in town, for instance: it still carries buses every day.
senses.exampleCN: 就拿镇上最老的那座桥来说，它如今每天仍承受公交车通行。
senses.why: Choosing one object and pointing at it is the oldest and most physical use of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 挑出一个对象并指着它，是这个短语最古老、也最具体的用法。

senses.title: A member used to explain a class
senses.definition: introduces a member of a category in order to explain what the category is
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个类别的成员，用来说明这个类别本身是什么
senses.example: A ruminant, for instance a cow, chews its food twice.
senses.exampleCN: 反刍动物，比如奶牛，会把食物咀嚼两遍。
senses.why: A definition becomes usable once a familiar member of the class is named.
senses.whyCN: 一个定义只有点出一个熟悉的成员，才变得可以操作。

senses.title: A case that tests a claim
senses.definition: used in argument to bring in a concrete case that supports or tests a general claim
senses.definitionCN: 在论证中引入一个具体事例，用来支持或检验一个普遍结论
senses.example: The rule fails, for instance, when two verbs share a single subject.
senses.exampleCN: 例如，当两个动词共用一个主语时，这条规则就会失效。
senses.why: Argument needs cases that can be checked, and the phrase hands one over for inspection.
senses.whyCN: 论证需要可核查的事例，这个短语正是把一个例子交出来供人检验。

senses.title: Casual illustration in speech
senses.definition: a relaxed spoken way of giving an example in conversation or in an interview
senses.definitionCN: 在对话或访谈中随口给出例子的轻松说法
senses.example: I like citrus fruit, for instance lemons and limes.
senses.exampleCN: 我喜欢柑橘类水果，比如柠檬和青柠。
senses.why: Spoken English prefers a short phrase to a written abbreviation, so the same words carry a lighter tone.
senses.whyCN: 口语更爱用一个短短语而不是书面缩写，因此同样的词语气更轻。

senses.title: One case among others
senses.titleCN: 只举一例、暗示还有更多
senses.definition: signals that the example given is not the only one and that others could be added
senses.definitionCN: 表明所举的例子并非唯一，还可以再举出别的
senses.example: Whole industries, for instance shipbuilding, depend on a handful of suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 整个行业，例如造船业，都依赖少数几家供应商。
senses.why: Singling out one case implies a set behind it, which is why the phrase often closes an open list.
senses.whyCN: 单挑一个例子就暗示背后还有一批，因此这个短语常用于开放式列举的末尾。

intro.en: For instance joins the Old English preposition for, meaning on account of or as regards, with instance, a noun borrowed through French from Latin instantia, a state of being present or pressing. The two words settled into a fixed English phrase for pointing at one case.
intro.cn: 这个短语由古英语中表「为了、就……而言」的介词，与一个经法语借自拉丁语、原义为「在场、紧迫」的名词合成；两词在英语中固定下来，用来指向一个事例。

items.en: For began as a preposition of cause and purpose, and it still introduces the ground or the aim of a statement.
items.cn: 这个词最初是表原因与目的的介词，至今仍用来引出理由或目的。

items.en: Instantia meant presence, urgency or insistence, from a verb meaning to stand upon or press.
items.cn: 该词意为在场、紧迫或坚持，来自表示「立于其上、逼近」的动词。

items.en: French narrowed the noun towards a pressing request and later a legal case; English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词收窄为紧急请求，后又指法律案件；英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: In English the noun came to mean an occurrence or an example, the very sense the phrase needs.
items.cn: 在英语里，这个词转而指一次发生的事或一个例子，正是这个短语所需的意思。

items.en: The combination settled as a discourse marker with no inflection; its exact first date in print is uncertain.
items.cn: 这一组合固定为话语标记，没有词形变化；其确切的书面首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it is common in speech and teaching prose, while the shorter twin dominates formal writing.
items.cn: 今天它常见于口语与教学文字，而另一个更短的近义说法在正式写作中占主导。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin noun or its family; the second group lists other ways of introducing an example.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁名词或其词族；第二组是引出例子的其他说法。

entries.definition: The standard written phrase for the same job, shorter and slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 做同一件事的书面标准短语，更短，也略正式。

entries.definition: The noun inside the phrase, naming an example or an occurrence.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的名词，指一个例子或一次发生的事。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun, used when several cases are named together.
entries.definitionCN: 该名词的复数，用来指同时举出的多个事例。

entries.definition: The verb built on the noun, meaning to represent something by a concrete case.
entries.definitionCN: 由该名词构成的动词，义为用一个具体实例来体现某事物。

entries.definition: Borrowed from the same Latin adjective, meaning immediate or pressing.
entries.definitionCN: 借自同一个拉丁形容词，义为立即的、紧迫的。

entries.definition: Names the specific item just referred to rather than illustrating a general claim.
entries.definitionCN: 用于点名前面提到的具体对象，而不是为总体说法举例。

entries.definition: Introduces examples that belong to a category, often more than one at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 引出一个类别的成员作例子，常一次给出多个。

entries.definition: Adds items that form part of a larger group without making them the whole group.
entries.definitionCN: 补上属于更大整体的若干项，并不把它们当作全部。

entries.definition: A verb phrase that announces an example is coming and makes it explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 一个动词短语，预告并明确表示接下来要举例。

entries.definition: A single example that strongly supports the point just made.
entries.definitionCN: 指有力支持前面论点的单一事例。

normalIntro.en: The phrase is literally for one instance: the preposition gives the purpose, the noun names the case.
normalIntro.cn: 字面就是「为了一个实例」：介词给出目的，名词点出那个事例。

normal.en: For one instance: you take one case and hold it up for the listener.
normal.cn: 为了一个实例：你拿起一个事例，举给听的人看。

normal.en: A circled example on the blackboard: the general rule first, the concrete case second.
normal.cn: 黑板上被圈出的例子：先有通则，后有具体事例。

normal.en: Compare it with the shorter written twin; speech often prefers this longer form.
normal.cn: 与更短的书面同义说法相比，口语更常用这个较长的形式。

normal.en: The noun is instance, so the phrase literally names one occurrence.
normal.cn: 名词是「实例」，所以这个短语字面上就指一次发生的事。

normal.en: It never inflects: the words keep the same order in every sentence.
normal.cn: 它从不发生词形变化，在任何句子里词序都不变。

abstract.en: An example is a small door cut into a large wall of explanation.
abstract.cn: 例子是在一大堵解释的墙上开的一扇小门。

abstract.en: One case can carry the weight of a whole rule, but only if it is chosen honestly.
abstract.cn: 一个事例足以承载一整条规则，前提是它被诚实地挑选。

abstract.en: To point at one thing is also to admit that many others exist.
abstract.cn: 指向一个事物，同时也就承认还有许多别的事物存在。

examples.en: For instance, the oldest trees in the valley survived the drought.
examples.cn: 例如，谷地里最老的树熬过了那场干旱。

examples.en: A good teacher offers one case, for instance a familiar machine, before giving the rule.
examples.cn: 好老师会先给出一个例子，比如一台熟悉的机器，再讲规则。

examples.en: Some birds, for instance the swift, spend almost all their lives in the air.
examples.cn: 有些鸟，例如雨燕，几乎一生都在空中度过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛因斯滕斯」——「佛」引出话头，「因斯滕斯」就是那一个实例：例如、比如

root: 由古英语表原因的介词「为了、就……而言」与经法语借自拉丁语、原义为「在场、紧迫」的名词合成；两词在英语中固定为话语标记，确切书面首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from one illustrative case to sentence-initial use, parenthetical use, a representative case, a class explained, a claim tested, spoken usage and an open list.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个说明性的实例出发，依次走向句首举例、插入语举例、举一例作代表、用成员说明类别、用实例检验结论、口语用法与开放式列举。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a general rule on the board, and one real case circled in chalk beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上的一条通则，旁边用粉笔圈出的一个真实事例。

branches.en: THE FIRST ILLUSTRATION: one case is offered, either after a general point or at the head of a sentence.
branches.cn: 最初的举例：提出一个例子，或跟在总体观点之后，或置于句首。

branches.en: ONE CASE INSIDE THE SENTENCE: a parenthetical example that hints at a larger set.
branches.cn: 句中一例：以插入语方式举出一个例子，同时暗示背后还有更多。

branches.en: THE CASE HELD UP: one object is selected and pointed at as the representative.
branches.cn: 被举起来的例子：挑出一个对象当作代表指给人看。

branches.en: THE CLASS MADE VISIBLE: a familiar member explains what the category means.
branches.cn: 让类别可见：用一个熟悉的成员解释这一类是什么。

branches.en: THE CASE UNDER TEST AND THE CASE IN TALK: argument checks a claim, conversation simply illustrates.
branches.cn: 受检验的例子与闲聊中的例子：论证用它检验结论，对话只是随手举例。

intro.en: The phrase has two parts: a native English preposition and a Latin noun that reached English through French. The phrase itself carries no derivational suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两部分组成：一个英语本土介词，和一个经法语进入英语的拉丁名词。短语本身不带派生词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the noun instantia and its verb instare; both underlie the English noun but neither survives as a free English word.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁词条是名词与它的动词，两者都是英语名词的来源，但都没有作为自由词留在英语里。

items.example: It still introduces purpose in fixed phrases.
items.exampleCN: 它至今仍在一些固定搭配里引出目的。

items.structure: English noun from French and Latin
items.example: The noun names the case itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指的就是那个事例本身。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语中该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It supplied the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁名词由它派生。

items.example: It marks position or pressure in the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 它在拉丁动词里标记位置或压迫。

items.example: It turns a participle into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成抽象名词。

items.example: The verb take plus the phrase singles out a case.
items.exampleCN: 「拿」这个动词加上该短语，就把一个例子单挑出来。

items.example: It does the same work with fewer letters.
items.exampleCN: 它做同样的事，用的字数更少。

items.example: Notes use the abbreviation, while running text usually spells the phrase out.
items.exampleCN: 注释里用缩写，正文里通常把短语写全。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词经法语借入，义为「实例；事例」
由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「用实例表示」
由该动词加名词词尾构成，义为「实例化」
由该名词加复数词尾构成，义为「多个实例」

definition_zh: 例如；比如；举例来说（多用于书面与正式场合）
definition_en: used to introduce an example of what has just been said, especially in writing
core_image: 报告页边一支箭头，从概括的句子指向一个具体案例
scene: 报告写到第三页时需要具体案例，作者在句首另起一行给出。For example, the coastal town lost two metres of beach in a decade.
sceneCN: 这里取第 2 个义项（句首用于书面说明与学术写作）；句意为例如，这座海滨小镇十年间失去了两米海滩。

pos.zh: 副词性短语：例如；比如；举例来说

collocations.phrase: for example in the case of

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「取出样本」的名词经法语进入英语，义为「例子；范例；榜样」
由该名词加复数词尾构成，义为「多个例子」
由同族拉丁词干加动词词尾构成，义为「举例说明；是……的典型」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词词尾构成，义为「举例说明；例证」
由同族词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「模范的；可作范例的」
由同族词干加名词词尾构成，义为「范例；典型」

senses.title: One case that shows the point
senses.definition: to name one case that shows what the previous statement means
senses.definitionCN: 举出一个事例，使前面的说法变得明白
senses.example: Some fuels burn cleanly; natural gas, for example, produces little soot.
senses.exampleCN: 有些燃料燃烧洁净，例如天然气产生的烟尘很少。
senses.why: The noun example names something taken out as a sample, so the phrase hands over one sample of the claim.
senses.whyCN: 「例子」本指被取出来作样本的东西，因此这个短语就是交出一个样本作证。

senses.title: Sentence-initial in written prose
senses.definition: placed at the head of a sentence in reports and academic writing
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用于报告与学术写作中
senses.example: For example, a two-line change in the code fixed the whole error.
senses.exampleCN: 例如，代码里改了两行就解决了整个错误。
senses.why: Written English likes a clear signpost at the start of the sentence, and this phrase supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 书面英语喜欢在句首放一个清楚的指路牌，这个短语正好充当。

senses.title: Parenthetical inside a clause
senses.definition: inserted between commas after a noun to add one illustrative case
senses.definitionCN: 用逗号插在名词之后，补上一个说明性的例子
senses.example: The older workers, for example the machinists, knew the old lathes best.
senses.exampleCN: 老工人，例如机械工，最熟悉那些旧车床。
senses.why: A parenthesis keeps the main clause intact while one case is slipped in beside it.
senses.whyCN: 插入语让主句保持完整，同时把一个例子塞到旁边。

senses.title: A typical representative
senses.definition: used of a case that is typical of its class rather than merely one of many
senses.definitionCN: 用于某一类中具有典型性、而非随便一个的事例
senses.example: A typical port, for example Rotterdam, handles millions of containers a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一座典型港口，例如鹿特丹，每年处理数百万个集装箱。
senses.why: Some examples are chosen because they are ordinary, and the phrase then carries the sense of a model case.
senses.whyCN: 有些例子之所以被选中，是因为它们平常而典型，此时这个短语带有「样板」的意味。

senses.title: Explaining a technical term
senses.definition: introduces a familiar instance that explains a technical name
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个熟悉的实例，用来说明一个专业名称
senses.example: A catalyst, for example platinum, speeds a reaction without being consumed.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂，例如铂，能加快反应而自身不被消耗。
senses.why: Technical writing defines by naming one known member, which is the work this phrase does.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作常用一个已知成员来下定义，这正是这个短语所做的事。

senses.title: Appositive specification
senses.definition: placed after a category noun to specify one member of it
senses.definitionCN: 放在类别名词之后，点明其中一个成员
senses.example: Root vegetables, for example carrots, store sugar underground.
senses.exampleCN: 根类蔬菜，例如胡萝卜，把糖分储存在地下。
senses.why: The phrase can act almost like a colon, turning a broad label into a visible object.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语几乎能起冒号的作用，把宽泛的标签变成一个看得见的对象。

senses.title: Illustration in a lecture
senses.definition: used in a talk to pause and place a concrete case before the audience
senses.definitionCN: 在讲演中稍作停顿，把一个具体案例摆到听众面前
senses.example: For example, imagine a queue at a single ticket window.
senses.exampleCN: 例如，设想只有一个售票窗口前的长队。
senses.why: A speaker needs to slow down and give the ear a picture, and the phrase marks that pause.
senses.whyCN: 讲者需要放慢速度给耳朵一幅画面，这个短语就标出那次停顿。

senses.title: Spelling out the written marker
senses.definition: used in formal prose instead of the abbreviated Latin marker found in notes
senses.definitionCN: 正式文章中把标记写全，而不用注释里的拉丁缩写
senses.example: Journals often spell out for example rather than use the abbreviation in running text.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊在正文里常把这个短语写全，而不用缩写。
senses.why: Running text avoids abbreviations that belong to notes, so the full phrase becomes the formal choice.
senses.whyCN: 正文回避属于注释的缩写，于是写全的短语成为正式选择。

intro.en: For example joins the native preposition for with example, a noun from Latin exemplum, something taken out as a sample, built on eximere, to take out. French carried the noun into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由本土介词与「例子」一词合成；后者出自拉丁语中意为「取出作样本之物」的名词，其动词意为「取出」，经法语进入英语。

items.en: For marked cause, purpose or the ground of a statement, a role it keeps in the phrase.
items.cn: 这个词标记原因、目的或立论的依据，这一角色在短语里保留至今。

items.en: Eximere meant to take out, from ex, out, and emere, to take or buy.
items.cn: 这个动词意为取出，由表示「向外」的前缀与表示「拿、买」的词构成。

items.en: Exemplum named a sample, a copy or a precedent, the thing taken out of a larger stock.
items.cn: 这个名词指样本、副本或先例，即从更大的一批中取出之物。

items.en: French reshaped the noun and passed it to English; the English spelling settled later.
items.cn: 法语改造了这个名词并传入英语，英语的拼写后来才固定。

items.en: English used the noun for a case that illustrates a rule; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用这个名词指说明规则的事例；其确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The phrase became the standard written marker for illustration, slightly more formal than its spoken twin.
items.cn: 这个短语成为书面举例的标准标记，比口语中的同义说法略正式。

note.en: The first group shares the noun or its word family; the second group names other ways of pointing to an instance.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个名词或其词族；第二组是指向实例的其他说法。

entries.definition: The same job in a slightly lighter, more conversational key.
entries.definitionCN: 做同一件事，语气更轻、更口语化的同义短语。

entries.definition: The noun inside the phrase, naming a sample or a model.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的名词，指样本或范例。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun, used when several cases are named.
entries.definitionCN: 该名词的复数，用来指同时举出的多个例子。

entries.definition: The verb built on the same stem, meaning to illustrate by example.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的动词，义为举例说明。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same family, meaning fit to serve as a model.
entries.definitionCN: 同族的形容词，义为可作模范的。

entries.definition: Introduces members of a category, usually with no comma before a short list.
entries.definitionCN: 引出类别的成员作例子，短列举前通常不加逗号。

entries.definition: Specifies exactly what was referred to, not merely one instance of it.
entries.definitionCN: 精确点明所指为何，而不只是给出其中一个实例。

entries.definition: Marks items as part of a larger set rather than as illustrations of a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干项标为更大集合的一部分，而不是作为规则的例证。

entries.definition: A verb phrase that announces illustration and ties it to the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 一个动词短语，预告举例并把例子与论证绑在一起。

entries.definition: One strong case offered as direct support for the point just made.
entries.definitionCN: 指有力支持前面论点的单一事例。

normalIntro.en: The phrase literally offers one sample taken out of a larger stock: for the purpose of showing a case.
normalIntro.cn: 这个短语字面上就是从更大一批里取出一个样本，用来展示一个事例。

normal.en: An arrow in the margin from a general sentence to one concrete case.
normal.cn: 页边的一支箭头，从概括的句子指向一个具体案例。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant a sample taken out of the heap, so the phrase lifts one case out.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词本指从一堆里取出的样本，所以这个短语是把一个例子拎出来。

normal.en: Written prose likes it at the head of the sentence, with a comma right after.
normal.cn: 书面文章喜欢把它放在句首，并在其后加逗号。

normal.en: It is the formal twin of the conversational phrase; the two do the same work.
normal.cn: 它是口语同义短语的正式版本，两者做同一件事。

normal.en: The words never change shape, whatever the sentence does around them.
normal.cn: 无论周围的句子怎么变，这两个词本身从不改变形态。

abstract.en: An example is a controlled experiment run inside an argument.
abstract.cn: 例子是在论证内部做的一次受控实验。

abstract.en: To illustrate is to lend one visible object to an invisible claim.
abstract.cn: 举例就是把一个看得见的物件借给一个看不见的论断。

abstract.en: The shorter the phrase, the more the writer trusts the reader to see the pattern.
abstract.cn: 短语越短，作者就越相信读者能自己看出其中的模式。

examples.en: For example, the oldest trees in the valley survived the drought.
examples.cn: 例如，谷地里最老的树熬过了那场干旱。

examples.en: A good report gives one case, for example a failed pump, before stating the rule.
examples.cn: 好的报告会先给出一个案例，比如一台失效的泵，再陈述规律。

examples.en: For example, the coastal town lost two metres of beach in a decade.
examples.cn: 例如，这座海滨小镇十年间失去了两米海滩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛 爱克桑普」——「佛」起话头，「爱克桑普」就是摆出来的那个样本：例如、举例来说

root: 由古英语表原因的介词「为了」与经法语借自拉丁语、原义为「取出作样本之物」的名词合成；固定短语的确切书面首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from one illustrative case to sentence-initial use, parenthetical use, a typical model, a term explained, an appositive, lecture illustration and the written marker itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从用一个例子说明观点，依次延伸到句首书面用法、插入语、典型代表、术语解释、同位语具体化、讲授举例与写全标记本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a margin arrow running from a general sentence to one concrete case.
core.cn: 核心意象：页边一支箭头，从概括的句子指向一个具体案例。

branches.en: THE TYPICAL CASE: one representative sample carries the general claim.
branches.cn: 典型例子：一个有代表性的样本承载总体说法。

branches.en: THE OPENING MOVE: the phrase starts a sentence in writing or in a lecture.
branches.cn: 开篇动作：在书面或讲授中把短语置于句首。

branches.en: THE CASE BESIDE THE NOUN: a parenthesis or an appositive narrows a broad label.
branches.cn: 贴在名词旁边的例子：插入语或同位语把宽泛标签具体化。

branches.en: THE TERM MADE PLAIN: a familiar instance explains a technical name.
branches.cn: 术语变得浅白：一个熟悉的实例解释专业名称。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN MARKER ITSELF: formal prose spells the phrase out instead of abbreviating.
branches.cn: 书面标记本身：正式文章把短语写全，而不用缩写。

intro.en: The phrase combines a native preposition with a Latin noun that came through French. Its parts are still transparent to a modern reader.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个本土介词与一个经法语而来的拉丁名词组合在一起，各部分对今天的读者仍然一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the verb eximere and the noun exemplum; the noun is the direct source of the English word example.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁词条是动词与名词，其中名词是英语「例子」一词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the phrase its purpose.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个短语提供目的。

items.structure: English noun from French and Latin
items.example: The noun carries the case being offered.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词承载被举出的那个例子。

items.meaning: a sample, a copy, a precedent
items.example: It is the direct source of example.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语「例子」一词的直接来源。

items.example: It built the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词构成了拉丁名词。

items.example: It marks the act of taking something out.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「把某物取出来」的动作。

items.example: It forms a neuter noun from a verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词词干构成中性名词。

items.example: The verb form does the work of the phrase in one word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用一个词完成了该短语的工作。

items.example: It does the same work in speech.
items.exampleCN: 它在口语中做同样的工作。

items.example: It belongs in notes rather than in running prose.
items.exampleCN: 它属于注释，而不属于正文。

latinEntries.meaning: a sample, a copy, a precedent

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词经法语借入，义为「例子；范例」
由同族词干加动词词尾构成，义为「举例说明」
由该动词加名词词尾构成，义为「例证」
由同族词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「可作模范的」

definition_zh: 而且；此外；再者（书面正式，表递进）
definition_en: used to add a further and usually stronger point to what has already been said, chiefly in formal writing
core_image: 评审表上第一条理由后面，又添上一条分量更重的新理由
scene: 评审意见先肯定方法可靠，随后又追加一条更有分量的理由。The method is reliable; moreover, it costs less than the old one.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（书面正式地递进补充第二点）；句意为这个方法可靠，而且比旧方法花费更少。

collocations.phrase: moreover, it should be noted that

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级演变而来，义为「更多；更」
本词后半，由古英语表示「在上、越过」的词演变而来，义为「在上方；越过」
与前半同词根的最高级形式，义为「最多；最」
由该最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多；主要地」

senses.title: Adding a further point
senses.definition: introducing an additional point that follows from or strengthens the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 引出另一点，它与前面的话相接或使前面的话更强
senses.example: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。
senses.why: More adds quantity and over adds going beyond, so the adverb literally places another point on top.
senses.whyCN: 前半表「更多」，后半表「越过」，所以这个副词字面上就是把另一点摞在上面。

senses.title: Adding a stronger reason
senses.definition: used to bring in a reason that carries more weight than the one before
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入一个比前一条更有分量的理由
senses.example: The witness was credible; moreover, her account matched the records.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人可信，而且她的陈述与记录相符。
senses.why: The word often marks not just addition but escalation, since the second point is meant to settle the matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常常不只表示添加，还表示加码，因为第二点意在把问题定下来。

senses.title: The second argument in a chain
senses.definition: introducing a parallel reason in a debate or a written argument
senses.definitionCN: 在论辩或书面论证中引入一条并列的理由
senses.example: The policy failed on cost; moreover, it failed on fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在成本上失败，而且在公平性上也失败。
senses.why: Written argument stacks reasons in order, and the adverb signals that the stack is still growing.
senses.whyCN: 书面论证把理由按顺序摞起来，这个副词表示这一摞还在加高。

senses.title: Supporting evidence in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术文本中补充同向证据
senses.definition: used in research writing to add confirming evidence in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中补上同方向的印证材料
senses.example: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
senses.exampleCN: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。
senses.why: Academic prose separates claims from support, and the word introduces a second piece of support.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把论断与支撑分开，这个词引出第二份支撑材料。

senses.title: Cumulative conditions in rules
senses.definition: used in regulations and contracts to add another condition that must also hold
senses.definitionCN: 在规章与合同里再添一项也必须满足的条件
senses.example: The applicant must hold a licence; moreover, the licence must be current.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须持有许可证，而且该证必须仍在有效期内。
senses.why: Legal drafting accumulates requirements, and each added clause must be met as well as the earlier ones.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草会累积要求，每添一条都与前面诸条同样必须满足。

senses.title: Sentence-initial link across sentences
senses.definition: placed at the start of a new sentence to tie it to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 放在新句子的开头，把该句与上一句绑在一起
senses.example: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。
senses.why: A connective at the head of a sentence tells the reader how the new sentence relates to the old one.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首的连接词告诉读者新句子与旧句子是什么关系。

senses.title: Rhetorical escalation in speeches
senses.definition: used in public speech to raise the force of an argument step by step
senses.definitionCN: 在公开演讲中一步步抬高论点的力度
senses.example: The city needs more homes; moreover, it needs them now.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市需要更多住房，而且现在就需要。
senses.why: Spoken rhetoric uses the heavy adverb to make the second clause sound like the decisive one.
senses.whyCN: 口头论辩用这个厚重的副词，让第二个分句听起来像是决定性的那一个。

senses.title: Heavier register than its synonyms
senses.titleCN: 比同义说法更书面的语体
senses.definition: used where a formal tone is wanted, in contrast with lighter everyday connectives
senses.definitionCN: 用于需要正式语体的场合，与更轻的日常连接词形成对照
senses.example: Moreover is common in reports, whereas the shorter synonyms suit speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法常见于报告，而较短的近义说法更适合口语。
senses.why: The word itself is a register signal: choosing it announces that the text is formal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就是语体信号：选用它就宣告文本属于正式文体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native English compound of more, the comparative of much, and over, used as an intensifier. It is not a Latin borrowing, so the Latin entry list is empty.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土复合词，由表示「多」的比较级与作加强成分的「在上、越过」合成，并非拉丁语借词，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.en: Māra was the comparative of the word for much, and it supplies the first element.
items.cn: 古英语中表示「多」的比较级提供了第一个成分。

items.en: Ofer meant over or beyond, and in compounds it adds the sense of going further.
items.cn: 这个词意为在上、越过，在复合词中增添「更进一步」的意思。

items.en: The two words first appeared as a phrase meaning beyond that, further, before they merged.
items.cn: 两词先以短语形式出现，义为「在那之外、更进一步」，后来才合并。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the merged adverb stood at the head of a sentence to add a point; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个合并的副词已站在句首用来追加论点；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it belongs to formal prose and public argument and sounds heavier than its shorter rivals.
items.cn: 今天它属于正式文章与公共论辩，听起来比更短的近义说法更重。

note.en: The first group shares the compound structure or the same root; the second group lists connectives that also add a point.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合结构或同一词根；第二组是同样用于追加论点的连接词。

entries.definition: A formal connective with the same job, built from further and more.
entries.definitionCN: 一个作用相同的正式连接词，由「更远」与「更多」构成。

entries.definition: The comparative that supplies the first half of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 提供这个词前半部分的比较级形式。

entries.definition: The second half, adding the sense of beyond or on top.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分，增添「越过、在上」的意思。

entries.definition: The superlative of the same root, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的最高级，义为最多。

entries.definition: An adverb from the same root, meaning for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的副词，义为大部分情况下。

entries.definition: A lighter connective that adds a point, often in speech and often with a hint of afterthought.
entries.definitionCN: 语气更轻的追加连接词，多用于口语，常带「顺带一提」的意味。

entries.definition: A plain phrase that adds an item without raising the tone.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的追加短语，只添一项，不抬高语气。

entries.definition: An emphatic phrase that adds a stronger consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 强调式短语，用来追加更有分量的考虑。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for one more point stacked on the rest.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示在其余之上再加一点。

entries.definition: An adverb that pushes the argument one step farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把论证再往前推一步的副词。

normalIntro.en: More plus over: one point is placed over and beyond the first, and the compound says exactly that.
normalIntro.cn: 「更多」加「越过」：把一点摞到第一点之上并越过它，这个复合词说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Stack two bricks: the second sits higher and presses the first down.
normal.cn: 两块砖叠起来：第二块位置更高，并把第一块压住。

normal.en: It always takes a comma right after it when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: 它放在句首时，后面总要跟一个逗号。

normal.en: In reports it replaces the spoken phrase for and also.
normal.cn: 在报告里，它替代口语中表示「而且还有」的说法。

normal.en: It never inflects; only its position in the sentence changes.
normal.cn: 它从不发生词形变化，变的只是它在句子里的位置。

normal.en: A reviewer writes it when the first reason was not quite enough.
normal.cn: 评审人写它，往往是因为第一条理由还不够。

abstract.en: A second reason is not a repetition; it is new weight on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 第二条理由不是重复，而是同一杆秤上新加的砝码。

abstract.en: Formal writing uses a signpost that admits it is adding something.
abstract.cn: 正式写作会用一块指路牌，坦白说明自己正在添加内容。

abstract.en: To say moreover is to promise that the next sentence earns its place.
abstract.cn: 说出这个词，就等于承诺下一句配得上它的位置。

examples.en: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
examples.cn: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。

examples.en: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
examples.cn: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。

examples.en: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
examples.cn: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「莫罗佛」——「莫」是更多，「罗佛」是越过去，多上加多、层层加码：而且、此外

root: 英语本土复合词，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级与表示「在上、越过」的词合成，十六世纪起用作句首副词；确切书面首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a simple added point through a stronger reason, a parallel argument, academic evidence, cumulative rules, sentence linking, rhetorical escalation and the word's own formal tone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯追加一点，依次走向更强的理由、并列论据、学术证据、累积条款、跨句衔接、修辞加码，最后落到这个词本身的正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a review sheet where a second, heavier reason is written under the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张评审表，第一条理由下面又写上了分量更重的第二条。

branches.en: THE ADDED POINT: a further statement is attached, often at the head of the next sentence.
branches.cn: 追加的一点：再添一句，常置于下一句句首。

branches.en: THE STRONGER PUSH: the new point carries more weight and raises the tone.
branches.cn: 更强的一推：新论点分量更重，也抬高语气。

branches.en: THE SECOND ARGUMENT: a parallel reason stands beside the first in a debate.
branches.cn: 第二条论据：论辩中与第一条并立的理由。

branches.en: THE EXTRA EVIDENCE: academic prose adds confirming data in the same direction.
branches.cn: 额外证据：学术文字补上同方向的印证数据。

branches.en: THE CUMULATIVE RULE AND THE HEAVY TONE: conditions stack in documents, and the word itself marks formal register.
branches.cn: 累积条款与厚重语体：文书里条件层层叠加，这个词本身就标记正式语体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native compound, so its parts are ordinary English words rather than affixes. The items below show the compound and its family.
intro.cn: 这是本族复合词，组成部分是普通英语词而非词缀。下列条目展示这一复合词及其词族。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: the word is built from Old English elements and has no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词条：这个词由古英语成分构成，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，清单按设计留空。

items.example: The compound itself adds a point.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词本身表示追加一点。

items.example: It supplies the first element.
items.exampleCN: 它提供第一个成分。

items.example: It supplies the second element.
items.exampleCN: 它提供第二个成分。

items.example: A parallel compound with the same function.
items.exampleCN: 一个功能相同的并列复合词。

items.example: It adds a point in a lighter tone.
items.exampleCN: 它以更轻的语气追加一点。

items.example: It shares the root of the first element.
items.exampleCN: 它与第一个成分同根。

items.example: The adverb ending turns the superlative into a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾把最高级变成修饰语。

items.meaning: at the head of a clause, with a comma
items.example: Position alone signals that a new point is coming.
items.exampleCN: 仅靠位置就能提示有新论点要来。

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，义为「更多」
同一词根的最高级，义为「最多」
由最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多」
本词后半，义为「在上；越过」

definition_en: as a result or consequence; in this way or manner
core_image: 断掉的桥与绕行的旧河道，两条线合成一条必经的路
scene: 暴雨把山道冲断，车队只能改走河谷里的旧路。The mountain road was washed out; thus, the convoy took the old valley route.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（因此、所以，表结果）；句意为山道被冲毁，因此车队改走了河谷旧路。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词词尾构成的诙谐或非正式变体，义为「如此」
由本词与表示「远、至此」的词构成的固定短语，义为「到目前为止」
由本词与表示「多」的词构成的固定短语，义为「就这么多」
由本词与两个指示成分构成的固定短语，义为「如此这般」

senses.title: Introducing a result
senses.definition: used to introduce a result that follows from what was just stated
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出由前面所述自然产生的结果
senses.example: The valve was closed; thus, no steam entered the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门已关闭，因此没有蒸汽进入罐体。
senses.why: The oldest sense of manner turned into a sense of consequence: the way things were left produced the next state.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的方式义转为结果义：事情被弄成那样，下一步状态便随之而来。

senses.title: In this way
senses.definition: in the manner or by the means just described
senses.definitionCN: 以刚刚描述的方式或手段
senses.example: The frame is welded thus, with one bead along each joint.
senses.exampleCN: 框架就是这样焊成的，每条接缝上走一道焊道。
senses.why: Manner is the word's original meaning, and it survives whenever the sentence describes how something is done.
senses.whyCN: 方式是这个词的本义，只要句子在描述事情怎么做，这层意思就还在。

senses.title: Up to this point
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase thus far to mean up to the present point
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定搭配，表示到现在为止
senses.example: Thus far the trial has produced no side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 到目前为止，这次试验没有产生副作用。
senses.why: The idea of reaching a point produced a phrase for how far matters have gone.
senses.whyCN: 「到达某一点」的想法，发展出表示事情进展到何处的固定搭配。

senses.title: Therefore in academic argument
senses.definition: marking the conclusion drawn from evidence in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中标示由证据推出的结论
senses.example: The data are consistent; thus the model can be accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 数据彼此一致，因此该模型可以接受。
senses.why: Research writing needs an unmistakable marker for inference, and this adverb supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要一个不含糊的推论标记，这个副词正好提供。

senses.title: Hence in a proof
senses.definition: introducing a step that follows necessarily from the previous line
senses.definitionCN: 引出由上一步必然得出的下一步
senses.example: Every term is divisible by three; thus the sum is divisible by three.
senses.exampleCN: 每一项都能被三整除，因此总和也能被三整除。
senses.why: Mathematics adopted the word because a proof is a chain in which each link follows from the one before.
senses.whyCN: 数学采用这个词，是因为证明就是一条每一环都由前一环导出的链。

senses.title: Accordingly in legal text
senses.definition: in statutes and contracts, marking a legal consequence that follows
senses.definitionCN: 在法规与合同中标示随之而来的法律后果
senses.example: The notice was served late and thus the claim was barred.
senses.exampleCN: 通知送达过晚，因此该项请求被排除。
senses.why: Law states cause and effect precisely, and the adverb marks the second half of that relation.
senses.whyCN: 法律要精确陈述因果，这个副词标记这一关系的后半段。

senses.title: So, in literary narration
senses.definition: in older or literary prose, describing the manner in which something was done
senses.definitionCN: 在较古旧或文学性的文字里，描述某事是怎样做成的
senses.example: He folded the letter thus and pressed the seal into the wax.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这样把信折好，把印章压进蜡里。
senses.why: Narrative keeps the manner sense alive by letting the word point at a gesture as it happens.
senses.whyCN: 叙述文字让这个词指着正在发生的动作，从而让方式义延续下来。

senses.title: So in summary
senses.definition: closing a line of argument by gathering the final point together
senses.definitionCN: 收束一段论证，把最后一点收拢起来
senses.example: Thus we may say that the two methods agree in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 由此可见，这两种方法在实际中是一致的。
senses.why: A closing word needs to sound like a conclusion drawn rather than a new claim, and this adverb does that.
senses.whyCN: 收尾的词听起来要像推出的结论而非新主张，这个副词正好如此。

intro.en: Thus is a native Old English adverb meaning in this way. It has no Latin ancestor; its earlier Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than attested.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土的古英语副词，意为「以这种方式」，没有拉丁语祖先；其更早的日耳曼语来源只有重构形式，缺乏直接文献。

items.en: Þus meant in this way and pointed at the manner of an action.
items.cn: 这个词意为「以这种方式」，指向动作的方式。

items.en: The deeper Germanic form is reconstructed from related adverbs and is not directly attested, so the earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 更早的日耳曼语形式由相关副词重构而来，没有直接文献，因此更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Spelling shifted to the modern shape, and the word kept its manner sense while gaining a result sense.
items.cn: 拼写转为今天的形态，词义在保留方式义的同时发展出结果义。

items.en: Prose began to use it for consequence as well as manner; the exact date of that shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 散文开始用它兼表结果与方式；这一转变的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Mathematics, philosophy and law each adopted the adverb as a fixed sign of consequence.
items.cn: 数学、哲学与法律各自采用这个副词，作为标示结果的固定记号。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal and academic writing, while speech prefers a shorter synonym.
items.cn: 它主要存活于正式与学术写作中，口语更爱用更短的近义说法。

note.en: The first group shares a form or a letter pattern; the second group lists other connectives of consequence.
note.cn: 第一组在形态或字母组合上相近；第二组是其他表示结果的连接词。

entries.definition: A demonstrative with the same opening letters, pointing at what is near.
entries.definitionCN: 开头字母相同的指示词，指向近处的事物。

entries.definition: A plural demonstrative that looks close on the page but means something far.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写看上去相近的复数指示词，意思却指远处的事物。

entries.definition: A humorous or informal adverb built by adding a suffix to the word.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加词尾构成的诙谐或非正式副词。

entries.definition: A time adverb that also begins with the same letters but marks sequence, not consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以这几个字母开头的副词，但标记时间顺序而非结果。

entries.definition: A noun for a heavy dull sound, close in spelling and sound but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉闷撞击声的名词，拼写与读音都近，但并无词源关系。

entries.definition: The most explicit connective of consequence, common in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 最明确的结果连接词，常见于正式文字。

entries.definition: A formal connective of consequence, often followed by a noun phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的结果连接词，后面常直接跟名词短语。

entries.definition: Marks a result with emphasis on the causal link.
entries.definitionCN: 标记结果，并强调因果联系。

entries.definition: Marks a result that calls for a matching response or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 标记结果，并暗示相应采取的行动或安排。

entries.definition: The short everyday connective of result, preferred in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 最短的日常结果连接词，口语中更常用。

normalIntro.en: Thus is the little arrow in formal prose: cause first, result after it, and a manner sense underneath.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是正式文字里的小箭头：原因在前，结果在后，底下还压着一层方式义。

normal.en: Hold your hand out thus: the word can still describe the way a thing is done.
normal.cn: 把手这样伸出去：这个词至今仍能描述一件事怎么做。

normal.en: Read it as a short so: cause, semicolon, result.
normal.cn: 把它读成一个短短的「所以」：原因、分号、结果。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases are thus far and thus much.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭配是表示「至今」与「这么多」的两个短语。

normal.en: In a proof it is the arrow saying the next line must follow.
normal.cn: 在证明里，它是一支箭头，表示下一行必须跟着成立。

normal.en: It has no ending and never changes shape.
normal.cn: 它没有词尾，也从不改变形态。

abstract.en: A word that means both therefore and in this way reminds us that causes and methods are often the same thing.
abstract.cn: 一个词兼表「因此」与「如此」，提醒我们原因与方法常常是一回事。

abstract.en: Formal writing uses it to admit that a step was taken, not merely asserted.
abstract.cn: 正式写作用它来承认某一步是被走出来的，而不只是被宣称的。

abstract.en: The shorter the connective, the more it trusts the reader to follow.
abstract.cn: 连接词越短，就越相信读者能自己跟上。

examples.en: The valve was closed; thus, no steam entered the tank.
examples.cn: 阀门已关闭，因此没有蒸汽进入罐体。

examples.en: The frame is welded thus, with one bead along each joint.
examples.cn: 框架就是这样焊成的，每条接缝上走一道焊道。

examples.en: Thus we may say that the two methods agree in practice.
examples.cn: 由此可见，这两种方法在实际中是一致的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「扎斯」——「扎」住前面的原因，「斯」就是随之而来的结果：因此、如此

root: 古英语本土副词，原义为「以这种方式」，兼指方式与结果；更早的日耳曼语形式仅有重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split into the two layers the word has always had: manner in one half, consequence in the other, with fixed phrases and formal registers in between.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分成这个词自古就有的两层：一半是方式，一半是结果，中间夹着固定搭配与正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken bridge and the old river road, two lines joined into one necessary route.
core.cn: 核心意象：断掉的桥与绕行的旧河道，两条线合成一条必经的路。

branches.en: THE RESULT: consequence is drawn both in everyday prose and in academic argument.
branches.cn: 结果：日常文字与学术论证中把结论引出。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the word shows how a thing is done, in technical or literary description.
branches.cn: 方式：在技术或文学描写中显示事情如何做成。

branches.en: THE POINT REACHED: a fixed phrase marks how far matters have gone.
branches.cn: 所到的这一步：固定搭配标示事情进展到何处。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CONSEQUENCE: a proof step or a legal effect follows of necessity.
branches.cn: 形式化的后果：证明的一步或法律效果必然随之而来。

branches.en: THE CLOSING WORD: a summary gathers its argument into one last line.
branches.cn: 收束之词：总结把论证收进最后一句。

intro.en: Thus is a native adverb with no affix of its own. The items below show its fixed phrases and the connectives it competes with.
intro.cn: 这是本族副词，本身不带词缀。下列条目展示它的固定搭配，以及与之竞争的连接词。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: the word descends from Old English and has no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词条：这个词源自古代英语，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，清单按设计留空。

items.meaning: in this way; as a result
items.example: The word carries both manner and consequence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时承载方式与结果。

items.meaning: in this way, humorous or informal
items.example: The suffix adds an adverb ending to an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给副词再加一层副词词尾。

items.example: The phrase limits the claim to the present.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把说法限制到眼下。

items.example: It measures the extent of what is said.
items.exampleCN: 它衡量所说内容的程度。

items.structure: English connective from a native root
items.example: It is the most explicit rival of thus.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词最明确的竞争者。

items.structure: English connective from a native root
items.example: It often leads straight into a noun phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它后面常直接接名词短语。

items.example: Speech prefers this short form.
items.exampleCN: 口语更偏爱这个短形式。

items.example: It stresses the causal link rather than the manner.
items.exampleCN: 它强调因果链，而非方式。

由本词构成的固定短语，义为「到目前为止」
由本词构成的固定短语，义为「就这么多」
由本词构成的固定短语，义为「如此这般」

definition_zh: 在……之前；先于；在……以前（较正式）
definition_en: before a particular time, event or action, used in formal and technical writing
core_image: 手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻
scene: 手术室外的推车停在门口，护士核对腕带与同意书。All patients must fast prior to the operation.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（在时间上先于某事件）；句意为所有病人都必须在手术之前禁食。

pos.zh: 介词性短语：在……之前；先于
相关形容词：先前的；优先的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语比较级形式，义为「先前的；在前的」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「优先；优先事项」
由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「按优先级排列；优先处理」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词词尾构成，义为「优先排序」
由同族名词加表示场所的词尾构成，义为「小修道院」

senses.title: Before a point in time
senses.definition: earlier than a stated time, date or event
senses.definitionCN: 早于某个指明的时间、日期或事件
senses.example: All applications must be filed prior to the first of March.
senses.exampleCN: 所有申请都必须在三月一日之前提交。
senses.why: Prior is the comparative of a word for before, so the phrase places one thing ahead of another on the timeline.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是比较级形式，词干意为「在前」，因此该短语把一件事放到时间线上另一件事的前面。

senses.title: Formal substitute for before
senses.definition: used in place of the plainer preposition in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中替代更朴素的介词
senses.example: Prior to the merger, the two firms were direct rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之前，这两家公司是直接的竞争对手。
senses.why: Documents often prefer a heavier phrase to a plain one, and this is the standard heavier choice.
senses.whyCN: 文书常用更厚重的短语代替朴素说法，这就是标准的厚重选择。

senses.title: Earlier in a procedure
senses.definition: marking the step that must be completed before the next one
senses.definitionCN: 标示必须在下一步之前完成的那一步
senses.example: The sample is weighed prior to drying.
senses.exampleCN: 样品在干燥之前先称重。
senses.why: A procedure is a sequence, and the phrase fixes which step comes first.
senses.whyCN: 流程是一个序列，这个短语固定了哪一步在前。

senses.title: Before doing something
senses.definition: followed by a gerund to name an action that must happen first
senses.definitionCN: 后接动名词，指出必须先发生的动作
senses.example: Prior to signing, read every clause aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 签署之前，把每一条款朗读一遍。
senses.why: The preposition takes a noun, so a verb must be turned into a gerund before it can follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词要接名词，所以动词必须先变成动名词才能跟在后面。

senses.title: Before a date in contracts
senses.definition: used in contracts to fix a deadline before a stated date
senses.definitionCN: 在合同中确定某一日期之前的期限
senses.example: Rent is payable prior to the fifth day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 租金须在每月第五日之前支付。
senses.why: Legal drafting needs a phrase that cannot be confused with after, and this one is unambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草需要一个不会与「之后」混淆的短语，这个短语毫不含糊。

senses.title: Before an observation in research
senses.definition: marking preparation that must precede measurement or testing
senses.definitionCN: 标示必须先于测量或测试完成的准备
senses.example: The instrument is calibrated prior to each run.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器在每次运行之前都要校准。
senses.why: Experimental method insists on order, and the phrase records that order in the protocol.
senses.whyCN: 实验方法强调次序，这个短语把该次序写进规程。

senses.title: Earlier in a sequence of events
senses.definition: used in narrative to place one event ahead of another
senses.definitionCN: 在叙述中把一件事放在另一件事之前
senses.example: The alarm sounded prior to the collapse, giving crews time to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 坍塌之前警报响了，为工人争取到撤离时间。
senses.why: Narrative uses the phrase to mark a warning that came early enough to matter.
senses.whyCN: 叙述用这个短语标记一个来得够早、因而起了作用的预警。

senses.title: Before arriving or departing
senses.definition: used of formal requirements that apply before a journey or an arrival
senses.definitionCN: 用于出发或到达之前必须满足的正式要求
senses.example: Passengers should check in prior to boarding.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客应在登机之前办理手续。
senses.why: Travel rules are written formally, and the phrase marks the deadline before the vehicle leaves.
senses.whyCN: 出行规定写得正式，这个短语标出交通工具离开之前的截止点。

intro.en: Prior comes from Latin prior, former or earlier, the comparative of a stem seen in prae, before. English first used it as a noun for a monastic superior and later as an adjective; the phrase prior to is a modern formal replacement for before.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「先前的、更早的」比较级形式，其词干见于表示「在前」的介词。英语先把它用作修院职名，后用作形容词；这个短语是近代对更朴素介词的正式替代。

items.en: Prae meant before or in front, and it is the stem behind the comparative prior.
items.cn: 这个词意为「在前、在……之前」，是比较级形式的词干来源。

items.en: Prior was the comparative of that stem, meaning former or earlier, and also a person set above others.
items.cn: 这个词是上述词干的比较级，意为先前的、更早的，也指位居他人之上者。

items.en: The Church used the noun for the head of a house, and French passed that noun to English.
items.cn: 教会用这个名词指修院之首，法语又把该名词传入英语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century English also used it plainly as earlier, beside the noun.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，英语也把它单纯用作「更早的」，与名词义并存。

items.en: The prepositional phrase spread in formal and legal writing in the nineteenth century; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个介词短语在十九世纪的正式与法律文书中扩散；确切的书面首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it is standard in documents, medicine and engineering, where the plainer word would sound too casual.
items.cn: 今天它常见于文书、医学与工程文本，在这些场合更朴素的近义介词显得太随意。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin comparative or its word family; the second group lists other ways of saying before.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁比较级或其词族；第二组是表示「在……之前」的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective inside the phrase, meaning earlier or more important.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的形容词，义为更早的或更重要的。

entries.definition: The noun built on the adjective, meaning first place or a matter ranked first.
entries.definitionCN: 由该形容词构成的名词，义为优先地位或首要事项。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to rank things in order of importance.
entries.definitionCN: 义为按重要程度排序的动词。

entries.definition: A religious house ruled by a prior, built on the older noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由更早的名词义构成，指由修院院长管理的小修道院。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning before, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「在前」的前缀，出自同一拉丁词干。

entries.definition: The plain everyday preposition that the phrase replaces in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的日常介词，正式文字中用该短语替代它。

entries.definition: A comparative phrase that compares two times directly.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级短语，直接比较两个时间。

entries.definition: A phrase for position in front, used of time as well as space.
entries.definitionCN: 表示位于前方的短语，时间和空间都可用。

entries.definition: An adjective for the thing that comes just before another.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指紧挨在另一事物之前的那一个。

entries.definition: A phrase stressing preparation made before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 强调在事件之前完成准备的短语。

normalIntro.en: Prior is the comparative of before: one thing stands ahead of another, and the phrase fixes that order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「在前」的比较级：一件事站在另一件之前，这个短语把这次序固定下来。

normal.en: A gurney at the theatre door while the clock is still one mark short of the start.
normal.cn: 手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻。

normal.en: Prior means earlier, so the phrase simply says earlier than a point.
normal.cn: 这个词意为更早的，所以短语就是「早于某一点」。

normal.en: In documents it replaces the plain word before and sounds more formal.
normal.cn: 在文书里它替代朴素的近义介词，听起来更正式。

normal.en: A verb after it must wear the ing ending, because a preposition takes a noun.
normal.cn: 它后面的动词必须加表示进行的词尾，因为介词要接名词。

normal.en: In contracts it usually points at a date, not at a person.
normal.cn: 在合同里它通常指向某个日期，而不是某个人。

abstract.en: To say prior to is to admit that order is part of meaning.
abstract.cn: 说「在……之前」，就是承认次序本身也是意义的一部分。

abstract.en: Formal language often pays for precision with extra weight.
abstract.cn: 正式语言常以更厚重的形式来换取精确。

abstract.en: Everything that must happen first is already a condition.
abstract.cn: 凡必须先发生的事，本身就已经是一个条件。

examples.en: All applications must be filed prior to the first of March.
examples.cn: 所有申请都必须在三月一日之前提交。

examples.en: The instrument is calibrated prior to each run.
examples.cn: 仪器在每次运行之前都要校准。

examples.en: Prior to signing, read every clause aloud.
examples.cn: 签署之前，把每一条款朗读一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普莱尔 图」——「普莱尔」是在前的，「图」朝向那一点：在……之前

root: 拉丁语比较级形式，义为「更早的、在先的」，词干见于表示「在前」的介词；英语先用作修院职名，后作形容词，短语为近代正式替代说法，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one core idea, earlier than a point, and vary the setting: plain time, formal prose, procedures, gerunds, contracts, experiments, narrative and travel.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个核心意思，即早于某一点，只是场景不同：单纯时间、正式文字、流程、动名词、合同、实验、叙述与出行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gurney waiting at the theatre door while the clock is still one mark short of the start.
core.cn: 核心意象：手术推车停在门口，墙上的钟还差一格才到开始时刻。

branches.en: TIME BEFORE: the phrase marks an earlier point and replaces the plainer word in formal prose.
branches.cn: 时间在先：标示更早的时点，并在正式文字中替代更朴素的说法。

branches.en: STEP BEFORE: in procedures and experiments one act must come first.
branches.cn: 步骤在先：流程与实验中，某一动作必须先做。

branches.en: ACTION BEFORE: a gerund names what must be done earlier.
branches.cn: 动作在先：动名词指出必须先做的事。

branches.en: DATE BEFORE: contracts fix a deadline by means of the phrase.
branches.cn: 日期在先：合同借这个短语设定截止期限。

branches.en: EVENT BEFORE: in a narrative the phrase places one event ahead of another.
branches.cn: 事件在先：叙述中把一件事放在另一件事之前。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin comparative adjective plus a native preposition. The items below show the family and the constructions it enters.
intro.cn: 这个短语由拉丁比较级形容词加本土介词构成。下列条目展示它的词族与它进入的结构。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are prior and the preposition prae; the related superlative primus explains the wider family but is not the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁词条是比较级形式与介词；相关的最高级形式解释了更大的词族，但并非直接来源。

items.example: It supplies the meaning of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个短语的意义。

items.example: It is the stem behind the comparative.
items.exampleCN: 它是比较级背后的词干。

items.example: It belongs to the same family but is not the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 它属于同一词族，但不是直接来源。

items.meaning: first place, a matter ranked first
items.example: It turns the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.meaning: to rank in order of importance
items.example: It turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成动作。

items.example: The action noun is built on the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词由动词构成。

items.meaning: a house ruled by a prior
items.example: It keeps the older noun sense of a superior.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了「上位者」这一较早的名词义。

items.example: The phrase takes a noun or a noun phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语接名词或名词短语。

items.example: A verb must become a gerund after the preposition.
items.exampleCN: 介词后的动词必须变成动名词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「优先；首要事项」
由该名词加动词词尾构成，义为「按优先级排列」
由该动词加名词词尾构成，义为「优先排序」
由同族名词加表示场所的词尾构成，义为「小修道院」

definition_en: after a particular event or time, used in formal, legal and technical writing
core_image: 竣工石碑立在路旁，压路机从碑后一路碾过去
scene: 验收会议结束之后，工程队才把最后一段路面铺完。Subsequent to the inspection, the crew paved the last stretch.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（在……之后，表时间先后）；句意为检查之后，施工队才铺完最后一段路面。

pos.zh: 介词性短语：在……之后；继……之后
相关形容词：随后的；后来的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语现在分词「随后而来的」经法语进入英语，义为「随后的；后来的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「随后；其后」
由表示「在下、随后」的前缀与表示「跟随」的词干加名词词尾构成，义为「后继；子序列」
由表示「跟随」的拉丁词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「继起的；继续的」
与上述词干同源的名词，义为「序列；次序」，并非由本词派生

senses.title: After an event in time
senses.definition: later than a stated event or point in time
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个指明的事件或时点
senses.example: Subsequent to the hearing, the court issued a written ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 听证之后，法院发布了书面裁决。
senses.why: The Latin participle means following after, so the phrase places one event behind another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「随后而来的」，因此这个短语把一件事放到另一件事之后。

senses.title: Formal substitute for after
senses.definition: used in place of the plainer preposition in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中替代更朴素的介词
senses.example: Subsequent to the merger, the two brands were kept separate.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之后，两个品牌仍各自保留。
senses.why: Legal and technical writing like a heavier connective, and this phrase is the standard one.
senses.whyCN: 法律与技术写作偏爱更厚重的连接词，这个短语就是标准选择。

senses.title: Immediately following in order
senses.definition: marking the next item or step in an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 标示有序系列中的下一项或下一步
senses.example: Subsequent to the first test, a second sample was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次测试之后，又取了第二份样品。
senses.why: Sequence is the word's core, so the phrase can mark order as well as simple time.
senses.whyCN: 「序列」是这个词的核心，所以这个短语既能标记时间，也能标记次序。

senses.title: After a date in contracts
senses.definition: used in contracts to fix the moment when a term begins to apply
senses.definitionCN: 在合同中确定条款开始适用的时刻
senses.example: Subsequent to the expiry date, the licence is void.
senses.exampleCN: 在到期日之后，许可证即失效。
senses.why: A contract must say clearly what happens after a date, and the phrase marks that side of it.
senses.whyCN: 合同必须清楚写明某一日期之后会发生什么，这个短语标记的就是那一面。

senses.title: In a later stage of a process
senses.definition: used of a stage that follows an earlier treatment or step
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项处理或步骤之后的后续阶段
senses.example: Subsequent to drying, the boards are sanded twice.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥之后，板材要打磨两遍。
senses.why: Production is a chain of stages, and the phrase names the link that comes later.
senses.whyCN: 生产是一串阶段，这个短语点出较后的一环。

senses.title: Following as a result
senses.definition: used when what follows is treated as a consequence of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 用于把随后发生的事当作前事的后果
senses.example: Subsequent to the leak, the plant was shut for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，工厂停产一周。
senses.why: The plain time meaning shades into cause when the later event is clearly produced by the earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 当后事明显由前事造成时，单纯的时间义就带上因果色彩。

senses.title: Later in a scholarly account
senses.titleCN: 学术叙述中的时间推进
senses.definition: used in historical or scientific writing to move the account forward
senses.definitionCN: 用于历史或科学写作，把叙述向前推进
senses.example: Subsequent to this period, pottery styles changed quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这一时期之后，陶器样式变化很快。
senses.why: Scholarship needs to mark periods in order, and the phrase carries the reader to the next one.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作需要按顺序标记时期，这个短语把读者带到下一个时期。

senses.title: Afterwards in a formal report
senses.titleCN: 正式报告中的事后说明
senses.definition: used in reports to record what was done after an earlier stage
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中记录某一阶段之后所做的工作
senses.example: Subsequent to the survey, three recommendations were drafted.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，起草了三项建议。
senses.why: Reports move from what was found to what was done next, and the phrase marks the second half.
senses.whyCN: 报告从发现写到随后所做之事，这个短语标记后半段。

intro.en: Subsequent comes from Latin subsequens, the present participle of subsequi, to follow after, from sub, under or close behind, and sequi, to follow. French carried the adjective into English, and the phrase subsequent to was built on it in modern formal prose.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语现在分词「随后而来的」，其动词意为「跟随在后」，由表示「在下、紧随」的前缀与表示「跟随」的词构成。法语把该形容词传入英语，这个短语则是近代正式文字在此基础上构成的。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it supplies the core of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为「跟随」，是这个词的核心来源。

items.en: Sub meant under or close behind, and here it adds the sense of coming after.
items.cn: 这个词意为「在下、紧随其后」，在这里增添「之后」的意思。

items.en: The verb and its participle named what follows on; classical Latin used them of time and of logic alike.
items.cn: 这个动词及其分词指随后而来者；古典拉丁语中既用于时间，也用于逻辑。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English, where its first date is not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传入英语，其在英语中的确切首见年代未见明确记载。

items.en: English used it for what comes later in time or in a sequence.
items.cn: 英语用它指在时间或次序上较后的事物。

items.en: The prepositional phrase belongs to modern legal and technical writing and replaces the plainer preposition.
items.cn: 这个介词短语属于现代法律与技术写作，用来替代更朴素的近义介词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of following or its word family; the second group lists other ways of saying after.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「跟随」的拉丁动词或其词族；第二组是表示「在……之后」的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective inside the phrase, meaning coming later.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的形容词，义为随后的。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning afterwards, used without a following object.
entries.definitionCN: 义为随后的副词，使用时后面不接宾语。

entries.definition: A noun for a later item or, in mathematics, a sequence drawn from another.
entries.definitionCN: 指后继项的名词，在数学中指从另一序列中取出的子序列。

entries.definition: A rare adjective from the same stem, meaning following on.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的罕见形容词，义为继起的。

entries.definition: A noun from the same stem, meaning order or a series, not derived from this word.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干名词，义为次序或序列，并非由本词派生。

entries.definition: The plain everyday preposition that the phrase replaces in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的日常介词，正式文字中用该短语替代它。

entries.definition: A preposition or adjective marking what comes next.
entries.definitionCN: 标记随后之事的前置词或形容词。

entries.definition: A comparative phrase that compares two times directly.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级短语，直接比较两个时间。

entries.definition: A phrase stressing that one event came right behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 强调一件事紧接另一件事而来的短语。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning after that, used without naming the starting point again.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「其后」的副词，不再重复起点。

normalIntro.en: Sub means close behind and sequi means to follow, so the phrase is a follower standing right behind an event.
normalIntro.cn: 前半意为紧随在后，后半意为跟随，所以这个短语就是一个紧站在事件后面的跟随者。

normal.en: A completion stone beside the road, and the roller moving on past it.
normal.cn: 竣工石碑立在路旁，压路机从碑后一路碾过去。

normal.en: Sub means under or close behind, and the word as a whole means following after.
normal.cn: 前半意为在下或紧随，整个词的意思就是跟随在后。

normal.en: In contracts it marks the date from which a term starts to run.
normal.cn: 在合同里它标出条款开始生效的那个日期。

normal.en: In reports it moves the reader from findings to what was done next.
normal.cn: 在报告里它把读者从发现带到随后所做的工作。

normal.en: A verb after it becomes a gerund, just as with its plainer synonym.
normal.cn: 它后面的动词要变成动名词，和更朴素的近义介词一样。

abstract.en: To say subsequent to is to insist that time has a direction.
abstract.cn: 说「在……之后」，就是在坚持时间有方向。

abstract.en: What follows an event is often what the event produced.
abstract.cn: 跟随在事件之后的东西，往往正是该事件的产物。

abstract.en: Formal prose pays for exactness with a longer phrase.
abstract.cn: 正式文字用更长的短语来换取精确。

examples.en: Subsequent to the hearing, the court issued a written ruling.
examples.cn: 听证之后，法院发布了书面裁决。

examples.en: Subsequent to the expiry date, the licence is void.
examples.cn: 在到期日之后，许可证即失效。

examples.en: Subsequent to the survey, three recommendations were drafted.
examples.cn: 调查之后，起草了三项建议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one direction, later than a point, and change the setting: plain time, formal prose, ordered sequence, contracts, processes, consequence, scholarship and reports.

branches.en: TIME AFTER: the phrase marks a later point and stands in for the plainer word.
branches.cn: 时间在后：标示更晚的时点，替代更朴素的介词。

branches.en: ORDER AND STAGE: next in sequence, or a later step in a process.
branches.cn: 次序与阶段：序列中的下一步，或流程的后续阶段。

branches.en: DATE AFTER: contracts fix the moment when a term starts to run.
branches.cn: 日期在后：合同确定条款开始生效的时刻。

branches.en: RESULT AFTER: what follows is treated as a consequence.
branches.cn: 结果在后：随之而来的事被当作后果。

branches.en: THE LATER ACCOUNT: scholarship and reports move the narrative forward.
branches.cn: 后来的叙述：学术与报告把叙述向前推进。

intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁现在分词与本土介词接在一起。下列条目展示它的词族与它进入的结构。
